sources.entry: How To Scrape With Python and Selenium WebDriver

summary.title: [Guide] Web Scraping 101: What you need to know and how to scrape with Python & Selenium Webdriver
summary.one_liner: You learn the basics of web scraping, its legal and ethical considerations, and how to scrape a GitHub project collection with Python, Selenium WebDriver and Pandas, exporting the results to CSV.
takeaways: Web scraping means programmatically extracting data from websites, useful when no API is offered.
Check a site's Terms of Service, robots.txt, and whether it offers an API before scraping; be gentle with request rates.
Selenium drives a real browser so it handles heavy JavaScript and clicks, but it is slow and memory-hungry when parallelized.
Selenium can find elements by XPath, read .text and get_attribute('href'), then store results in a dict and export via Pandas to CSV.
ProcessPoolExecutor can scrape several pages at once, each with its own browser instance.
summary.summary: The article opens with the legal and ethical side of web scraping, listing steps to check terms of service, robots.txt, APIs and contacting site owners. It then weighs Selenium WebDriver's pros (real browser, JavaScript support, human-like interaction) against its cons (slow, RAM-heavy in parallel). The tutorial walks through scraping the top machine learning projects from a GitHub collection: setting up ChromeDriver, locating <h1> elements by XPath, building a dictionary of names and URLs, and saving them to CSV with Pandas. It closes with a tip on parallelizing scraping with concurrent.futures and a note about possibly trying headless Chrome.
